text:
sam: Heads up — finance asked for a consistent error budget export they can include in the monthly ops report. Right now we have 3 different CSVs and a manual calc. Can we standardize the format from Grafana/Prometheus and include burn rate, remaining minutes, and incident links?
li: +1. We should also agree the canonical SLIs first so the numbers mean the same thing across teams.
maya: Quick proposal: 1) Availability SLI = successful_responses / total_requests (status 2xx/3xx) over rolling 30d. 2) Latency SLI = p95 inference latency for req_size<=512 tokens. 3) Saturation SLI = p95 GPU_utilization on serving pool. Thoughts?
jordan: Those look reasonable. For availability we need to exclude scheduled maintenance windows, and for dedicated customers we should compute separately (different error budgets).
li: For the export format, how about a single-line CSV per service with fields: service, sli_type, window_days, slo_target_pct, error_budget_minutes, consumed_minutes, burn_rate_1h, burn_rate_24h, grafana_panel_url, incidents[] (comma-separated short links). That will be easy for finance to ingest.
maya: Example numbers: SLO target 99.9% over 30d -> error_budget_minutes = 30*24*60 * 0.001 = 43.2 -> round to 43.
li: Yes. And we should include the raw PromQL we used to compute the SLI in the export so auditors can verify.
sam: Can we compute consumed_minutes from Prometheus directly? What's the PromQL for availability?
jordan: We derive availability by counting failing request seconds. Rough PromQL: ```sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api",code=~"5.."}[1m])) by (service) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api"}[1m])) by (service)``` then convert ratio->minutes over window. But we actually evaluate over sub-windows and count time where error_rate > threshold.
li: For latency SLI: ```histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="inference"}[5m])) by (le, service))``` Then aggregate into minutes where latency > threshold.
maya: For saturation: ```quantile_over_time(0.95, gpu_utilization{pool=~"serving.*"}[1h])``` and flag minutes where p95 > 85%.
ops-bot: Reminder: when you export incidents[] include only postmortems or incident thread links, not full text. Use the internal short link format: https://redwood.internal/incident/INC-1234
monitoring-bot: Current burn snapshot for api-service (30d window): error_budget_minutes=43, consumed=12, burn_rate_1h=0.8x, burn_rate_24h=1.3x, status=OK :thumbsup:
sam: OK, so action items: 1) standard CSV schema + sample export; 2) add raw PromQL lines into grafana panel metadata; 3) template export job (weekly+on-demand) that writes to S3 and triggers a slack summary. Who wants to own the PR?
li: I can draft the CSV schema and put a Grafana dashboard panel JSON with the PromQL bits.
jordan: I'll wire up a small exporter job (k8s CronJob) that runs the queries and emits the CSV to s3. Will include the per-customer split option.
maya: We should also add a conservative smoothing window when computing consumed_minutes so short spikes don't eat too much budget. E.g., only count a minute as "bad" if the p95 latency > threshold for 3 consecutive 1m buckets.
li: Good call. That reduces noise. Also add a column 'counting_policy' in the CSV: "3-of-3 1m windows" or similar.
sam: For thresholds — propose: availability target 99.9% (as discussed), latency p95 < 200ms (small requests), saturation p95 < 80% for serving pool. If saturation crosses 85% for >30m we should page ops.
jordan: Agree but add region nuance — some regions (eu-west-2) have fewer GPUs, so saturation threshold maybe 75% to trigger earlier scaling. We'll include region tag in the CSV.
li: What about burn-rate alerts? We should surface a grafana alert when 1h burn_rate > 8x and 24h burn_rate > 2x (these are the usual SLO escalation tiers). 8x for immediate paging, 2x for auto-ticket.
maya: +1. Also include predicted time-to-zero (time until error budget exhausted) in the export: minutes_remaining / (consumed_minutes_per_minute). It's helpful for on-call.
sam: Do we want to store the historical exported CSVs? Finance likes month-over-month. Keep them in s3 with lifecycle.
li: Yes — s3://redwood-ops/errorbudgets/YYYY-MM/service.csv and a small manifest file. We'll attach a signed URL in slack summary.
monitoring-bot: Alert: api-service burn_rate_1h=9.3x -> paging threshold exceeded. Link: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/abcd/slo-views?panelId=7 :rotating_light:
sam: Jumping in — ops team please investigate. Jordan, prioritize scaling check and recent deploys. Maya, validate if this is noise vs real. Li, start the export with current snapshot and attach to incident.
jordan: I'm on it. Showing increased queuing on node gpus-3 in us-west-2. Scaling policy didn't kick due to quota. Opening a service ticket to cloud for quota bump.
maya: Traces show a spike from a customer test harness — I'll throttle that tenant and re-evaluate.
li: I've pushed a first-draft CSV schema to the docs PR: https://git.internal/redwood/docs/pull/234 — includes sample rows and prometheus snippets.
sam: Perfect. After the incident, let's retro on whether our counting_policy gave the right signals. If not, adjust before we ship the export. :+1:
